_meta.purpose: Module-code PREFIX -> subject label, for the prefixes the All_Template_Reports learning-area folders do NOT file. build_granular_registry.py build_subject_map() reads the report folders FIRST (the standing source — a report-derived label is never overridden here) and then fills the remaining gaps from `prefixes` below. The merged map is written into Module_Structure_Index.json (_meta.subject_map + every module_meta.subject) and Granular_Scaffold_Registry.json (_meta._subject_map, the cascade's subject grouping). The subject label is what the HTML Generator's Reference-module Subject filter shows; a prefix absent from both sources keeps a blank subject (shown under 'All subjects', never offered as a filter entry — Gavin: no 'Unclassified').

Labels follow the library's existing precedent: a code filed under `Online > NCEA1` on the server is 'NCEA1' whatever its learning area (AGH / ART / HES / HIS / PES / PHE / PWO are already filed that way); a Te ara Tipu (Primary) learning area is its '1-10 <area>' folder name; the Style_Anchor_Registry's existing '1-10 Languages' subject (r265, CHFUN) takes the Phase 1-4 language families. Change a label here and re-run `python3 build_granular_registry.py --merge` — the label is output-inert for the current corpus (the cascade's engine application is OFF, and no shipped subject-keyed rule names these labels), so no regeneration follows a relabel.
